setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): By the first solo the hiss gets lost in furious jamming; Reviewer says the Scarlet/Fire pairing is short but excellent [29][30]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (2 reviews): Stranger doesn't end with the usual three-beat rhythm, easing instead directly into Terrapin Station in a unique transition; Stranger eases into Terrapin without the usual three-beat ending, which the reviewer finds unique [26][30]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Reviewer describes the Cassidy as haunting [20]
- **It's All Over Now** (1 review): Reviewer calls the first-set It's All Over Now an all-timer [30]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): Reviewer calls Big Railroad Blues a treat [23]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Reviewer calls the first-set Music Never Stopped truly great [26]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Reviewer says Garcia ends it by turning up and letting feedback rip, unusually [23]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): Some consider this the best version of the Brent era; reviewer agrees [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-05-11.mtx.dusborne.126880.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 164 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd80-05-11.sbd.nawrocki.13087.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 156 min; rated 3.71/5 by 7 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer hears a lot of tape hiss on this matrix recording; Reviewer says it may once have been pristine soundboard but is no longer, and doesn't recommend it for evaluating the show; Reviewer found the matrix tape quality poor and not matching memories of a hot show [21][22][24]
- **gd1980-05-11.sbd.miller.89577.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 156 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [4]. Said about its sound: This soundboard is the cleanest of the bunch but still hissy; second set sounds better [29]
- **gd1980-05-11.sbd.terrapinstation.tetzeli.fix-12259.33501.reflac.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 158 min [5]
- **gd1980-05-11.fob.glassberg.motb-0052.97522.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 162 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [8]. Said about its sound: Sounds slightly muted, as if the left microphone were obstructed; panning reduced but didn't eliminate it [8]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended and says the first set ran eleven songs, with Garcia playing very strongly [19]
- Reviewer calls it a Mother's Day show [26]
- Reviewer describes the pre-show scene outside the Civic Center: bikers, vendors, and wide-eyed fans; says Garcia's voice growled [28]
- Reviewer says it is overshadowed by the previous night but rivals Nassau, Rochester, Lewiston, Halloween and Gainesville from 1980 [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-05-11.mtx.dusborne.126880.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Dave Usborne; source: 2 Source Matrix By Dave Usborne;soundboard (shnid:89577); Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller;Recording Info:SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette -> Dat ->… [1]
- **gd80-05-11.sbd.nawrocki.13087.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Reviewer doubts Dick used gear giving a second-generation cassette this quality, suspecting additional analog generations in the lineage [22]
- **gd1980-05-11.sbd.miller.89577.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD [4]. Also: Soundboard is patched from a Nakamichi 700 audience source by Steve Rolfe, with channels swapped fixed and pitch corrected [4]
- **gd1980-05-11.sbd.terrapinstation.tetzeli.fix-12259.33501.reflac.flac16**: transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: SHN (12259) -> wav (CE Pro) -> flac (Trader's Little Helper) [5]. Also: Patches from the Rolfe audience source (Nak 700 to Sony D5) fix cuts and song endings in the soundboard [5]
- **gd1980-05-11.fob.glassberg.motb-0052.97522.flac16**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Adam Egert; source: FOB: 2 x Nakamichi CM700 => Sony TC-D5 >> MAC [8]
